title: Playing at the Moulin Rouge during the war and resisting the union
summary: He played racetrack Saturdays and nightly dance jobs at the Moulin Rouge, naming his sidemen, and refused pressure to join the union.

story.theme_name: Coming to New York: clubs, jams, and making it
story.community_name: Making it in New York: arrival, clubs and the scene

blocks.x: Who did you have in the band?
Joe James, or Bikes, Albert Jackson. What instrument did he play?

Yeah. T. Rouch, or no, no, I mean not him. Bikes. And that boy would do Rodney, that boy plays. He was playing. Then I had with the chorus playing, you know, he play with Fat Domino now. He used to play guitar. He played bass with Fat Domino. Little short fella. Oh I know, Jimmy Davis. Yeah, Jim. From up to Carrollton. Yeah, little Jim. Little Jim played with us a long time. And then on his rope rope. He told me that you told me. Yeah, on his rope rope, playing with me there. You know what I mean? But I'll tell you one thing, look. You see people, I'll tell you the truth. You know some people think you're really dumb. You know what I tell people? I say look, I may look dumb, but I ain't all that dumb. You know what I mean? I just said listen. Look, we playing at the Moulin Rouge, the union, you see the union was after us, you see. Man, it's so simple. It's so simple. You know what I'm usually, you know. Man, they really want to get that union. I told them boy, I said man I don't want to get no union. I said we got more job and we can play and we got a job to give them. You know what I mean? So the man said, man, you ought to get in the union. So he keep talking to me so that, you know. It was a long time before I met with my minor. Because we had to play to work, you know what I mean? We played all the time in any different other place, you know what I'm talking about? So we played there most every night playing in the Moulin Rouge. And you know how you keep up with songs? People come at you. People say, you got such a number? You may say, well no I don't have it. Next time I come back. That's how we used to do it. See when somebody come at me, you say, kid say you got such a number? I say no. See when I go back there next Saturday, I got that number. See? I go by. I keep up with me. I got a lot of truth kids back there, all kinds of songs. Very nice songs back there. You know what I mean? My truth kids. So that's how I used to keep up. You know, look, quite nasty, you couldn't go there and play there all the time, the same number over and over, you know. You see? Because people ask you for the different number, and then don't take that number and they don't want to hear that number, you know what I mean? They won't hear it you know. Oh yeah, sure. And I didn't hear people say, man that band's sick, they can't play nothing, they play the same thing over and over, you know what I mean? You got to change, you know what I mean? You got to change, you know what I mean? You got to change man. So, well we had two saxophones. Oh yeah? Yeah. That's when I tell you what Andrew played. Andrew played in the band with her. Russ played drum, bass player. Andrew? Yeah, but then we split the band up. I got out of that band. See? I got out of that band. They went to that set thing, you see? So Russ played with me, Andrew Morgan, all the other people. Well they used to go, I want to show how people try to double cross you, they didn't hurt you. That band, now that band, I come here and find this band, you see? I done built the band up, you see? You know what I mean? We used to go down the fire, the lockport everywhere. So them fellas tried to double cross me, you see? They thought I couldn't get no other band. I said, man I can get anybody. I can go to heaven and get people out of heaven. I said, you know what I mean? So all that. So they tried to have another band. So man, they went and started going all down the fire, and they started knocking. You know the man people told him that? He said, man, you all can't knock. Kid is the one built your door. Yeah, he said, you all can't do that band, nothing. You know what I mean? So look, that man wouldn't have no more. That's right. See? And so that's why Andrews was playing, but Ross, he played trumpet in the band. He played trumpet too, trumpet, drum and bass. But they had this band. It didn't last long. So finally, he spent at the Muno Rouge. His first dance all he had was the Rose Room. Right there where Dick was talking about, Carl, the second line, right there. He had the Rose Room. And I tell you, the first time we started playing there for Speck, it was a house and a grocery. So we were boo-legged liquor them days, them times. So me Wilford, George James, three of us played in the room. So Speck, what Speck would do, Speck would give a little party like this Saturday. All right. So next Saturday, no, for about three or four weeks he'd give these parties for color. For the month maybe, you see? All right. Then he'd turn around and he'd give a party for white. You know what he's doing? A lot of people didn't understand what a man would do, but I know what a man would do. He wanted to see which race he could make the most business of, white or colored, for that corner there. You know what I'm talking about. I don't know whether your father or white would be a better place for white. You see? So we still played in that man. Then he started, well, and Benny's making the bill up, you know then. Speck said, man I need a dance hall now. So this man would own the place, he was Italian. So anyhow, Speck asked him, was building a dance hall for him, so he said he didn't have the money. So the fella had the milk there where Dick was talking about, the man told Speck, he said, I'll build your dance hall on that side of the highway. You know what I mean? So then Speck got the money and they built this room. You see? They built this room where we played, I played there. So finally when I left from there, well that was where this boy went there and played. They was playing there when he was playing at the Moulin Rouge. They double-crossed Speck. The man, after the man had got his money, you know what I mean, and Speck got his money out of the man. So the man sold that place, another white fella. And that's why it made Speck have to build this other dance hall in Moulin Rouge. Because the man sold out on him. They don't even know anybody, you know what I'm talking about? So anyhow, so well them boys they played there a long time, and what you call his playing, at the coconut grove. But that boy named him again, hunting the doggy.
